messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: continuous-batch service group `cb/core` - p95 token latency breached (2.4s > 1.0s). Elevated queue depth and KV-cache eviction spikes observed. SEV2. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/ops/cb/core

emma: seeing same in us-west1. queue depth ~600, microbatch pileups.
matt: i'm on it, grabbing logs and ps on nodes. suspecting KV-cache blowup after last runtime tweak.
sophia: FYI rolled a prefetch coalescing tweak at ~03:02 UTC (prefetch.coalesce=true) to reduce small-request overhead. might be interacting with high concurrency.
paul: CS: two paying customers on dedicated reported timeouts and 5xxs starting ~03:05 UTC. escalations incoming.
linda: telem quick glance: token distribution shifted — more long sequences, KV entries per request up 4x on average.
matt: sounds like repeated long contexts + coalesced prefetch causing larger per-request KV state -> eviction churn -> backpressure -> queue growth.
emma: what's the minimal safe hotfix? we can revert prefetch coalesce and tighten microbatch windows.
sophia: recommend emergency runtime flags (canary first):

```
# emergency hotfix flags
--prefetch.coalesce=false               # revert the heuristic
--continuous_batch.max_microbatch_tokens=128
--continuous_batch.max_window_ms=20
--kvcache.eviction_pressure=0.7
--cb.throttle_latency_target_ms=200     # more aggressive throttling under latency pressure
```

matt: agree. also add `cb.dynamic_shrink=true` temporarily to reduce microbatch sizes under load.
emma: i'll kick a 10% canary rollback to prior prefetch behavior now. @matt monitor telemetry.
incident-bot: Deploy triggered by @emma: canary rollout 10% -> cb-runtime-config v2026.3.18-hotfix. CI: green.
matt: canary hosts show queue depth dropping ~40% after config flip. KV growth rate on canary decreased. :eyes: 
sophia: p95 latency on canary down 2.4s -> 1.1s within 2 minutes. promising.
paul: CS: partial relief reported — one tenant's timeouts dropped, others still tailing.
emma: ramping to 50% now. keeping a short observation window.
matt: telemetry: error rate trending down, but a few nodes still show elevated swap due to prior evictions. enqueue gating should help.
incident-bot: Canary at 50% -> monitoring for 5m.
emma: rolling to 100% at 03:28 UTC.
incident-bot: Rollout completed to 100% -> v2026.3.18-hotfix.
linda: post-rollout metrics: global p95 stabilized ~1.0s, error rate back to baseline. KV eviction spikes reduced.
paul: CS: notifying affected customers now; offering follow-up postmortem and mitigation timeline.
sophia: next steps (short): add a circuit-breaker on KV growth, dynamic microbatch shrink improvements, and perf regression tests for prefetch coalescing under high concurrency.
emma: creating follow-up ticket ENG-XXXXX to track root cause, test coverage, and safer rollout gates for prefetch heuristics.
matt: putting a temporary alert on KV growth rate and queue-depth/latency correlation so we get earlier detection.
paul: capturing affected customer list and timestamps for support.
emma: handing over on-call to @matt for the rest of the shift. please include timeline, actions taken, and any lingering customer remediation in the incident doc.
matt: acknowledged, taking over. will draft an incident summary and required action items.
linda: noted: add perf test that simulates many long-context concurrent requests to exercise KVC cache growth.
paul: thanks team — CS will follow up with customers in next 30m. :thumbsup:

-- brief notes --
- Root cause hypothesis: prefetch coalescing change increased per-request KV allocation under high concurrency and long-sequence workloads, triggering eviction churn and queueing cascades.
- Hotfix: revert prefetch.coalesce and tighten continuous-batch window + microbatch tokens, plus aggressive throttle.
- Customer impact: transient increase in timeouts/5xx for some dedicated tenants (~25% spike in errors during peak).
- Owner (postmortem): @emma -> ticket ENG-XXXXX; oncall handoff -> @matt.

incident-bot: Incident CLOSED -> mitigation stable for 30m. Follow-up: create postmortem and link action items. :white_check_mark:
